findings.title: 60s eligibility cache is stale, never invalidated, and runs before the cheap dataset check
findings.body: The allowlist result is cached for 60s per (org, hash of project ids). `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but never called, so removing a project from `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` keeps returning upsampled counts for up to a minute. `options.get` is already served from an in-process cache, so the extra cache round trip buys little. The cache lookup and write also happen before `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`. Every stats request on transactions, spans or metrics therefore pays a cache get and set for a decision that can never be True. The key also uses `hash(tuple(...))` instead of the ids themselves, so two different project sets can collide and share a wrong cached result. Do the dataset check first, and either drop the cache or invalidate it from the option-change path with an explicit id-based key.

findings.title: Substring match on raw request query misclassifies negated and mixed queries as error-only
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns True if the lowercased `query` GET param contains the substring `event.type:error`. That also matches `!event.type:error`, `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, and any value that merely starts with `error`. Queries that exclude errors or include transactions are then upsampled. `sum(sample_weight)` is meaningless or zero for transactions, so those counts come out wrong. A proper parse of the search filters is needed instead of a substring test.

findings.title: Upsampling check uses outer `dataset` and raw request query instead of the scoped dataset and actual query
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` and a possibly rewritten `query`, but the eligibility check passes the closure variable `dataset` and reads `request.GET['query']` inside the helper. In the dashboard-widget split flow the function is called with `discover` and `(query) AND !event.type:transaction`, or with `scoped_dataset` for the transaction-like split. The decision is then made against the original dataset and query, not the ones actually executed. The error-only split query on a metrics-enhanced request is never upsampled, so the counts differ from the same query run directly. The helper should take the scoped dataset and the query actually being run.

findings.title: upsampled_count uses sum(sample_weight) with no fallback for missing weights
findings.body: `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` returns 0 or undercounts for any error row where `sample_weight` is NULL, 0 or absent. That includes events ingested before the column was populated and events from allowlisted projects whose SDK sends no client sample rate. The code comment says the column is assumed to exist for all events, but nothing enforces it. For those rows the chart count becomes lower than the real `count()`, so it is a silent regression. Use something like `sum(coalesce(sample_weight, 1))`, or keep `count()` when weights are missing.

findings.title: upsampled_count is a public query function but references a column absent from non-error datasets
findings.body: Unlike the neighbouring function marked `private=True`, `upsampled_count` is publicly selectable by users. It depends on the `sample_weight` column, which the transactions dataset does not have, as the PR's own helper docstring says. A user calling `upsampled_count()` against transactions through the shared discover config will get a Snuba error. It should be private, or restricted to the errors dataset.

findings.title: RPC upsampling branches are dead code
findings.body: `use_rpc` is only true for `spans_rpc` and `ourlogs`. `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns False for every dataset other than errors and discover. The `upsampling_enabled` branches in the RPC and RPC top-events paths can therefore never run. The `upsampled_count() as count` string is also not a valid RPC y-axis. The branches add misleading code and should be removed.

findings.title: Docstrings and comments contradict the actual caching behaviour
findings.body: `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` says it reads the allowlist fresh each time to always have the latest configuration. Its only caller caches the result for 60s, so the statement is false. The endpoint comments ("This cached result ensures consistent behavior", "most current schema assumptions", "better query optimization and caching") describe nothing the code does and mislead maintainers.

findings.title: Trailing whitespace in new code
findings.body: Whitespace-only lines with trailing spaces were added in the endpoint (around lines 223, 234, 278) and throughout `error_upsampling.py` docstrings and blank lines. This will fail the repo's formatting and lint hooks (black, flake8 W291/W293).

findings.title: Stray submodule pointer committed
findings.body: A `sentry-repo` gitlink pointing at the base commit is added. It has nothing to do with the feature and looks like an accidental artifact of the working setup. It should be removed from the PR.

findings.title: Core eligibility function, cache behaviour and edge cases are untested
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` is not unit-tested, including its cache hit, miss and invalidation paths. Nothing covers `!event.type:error` or mixed queries, the top_events path, or the dashboard-split path. `self.snuba_params` is built in `setUp` but never used. The endpoint tests rely on freshly created project ids to avoid cache pollution rather than clearing the cache.

findings.title: Test helper swallows all exceptions and skips a zero rate
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` wraps lookups in bare `except Exception: pass`, which hides malformed contexts (for example `contexts: None`) and bad rates. `if client_sample_rate:` also ignores a legitimate value of 0. It runs on every `store_event` call and mutates the normalized payload for all tests that set `contexts.error_sampling`, which is a broad side effect for a fixture helper.
